summary: The Kansas City Chiefs beat the New York Jets 23-20 on NBC's "Sunday Night Football" at MetLife Stadium on Oct. 1, 2023, after leading 17-0 and letting the Jets tie it at 20 entering the fourth quarter. A Zach Wilson fumble and a Harrison Butker field goal decided it, while Patrick Mahomes threw two interceptions but made clutch plays. The note includes a live blog, broadcast info and Taylor Swift's attendance.
one_line: Chiefs held off a Jets comeback to win 23-20 on Sunday Night Football on Oct. 1, 2023, with Mahomes and Pacheco leading the way.
key_facts: The Chiefs beat the Jets 23-20 on Sunday, Oct. 1, 2023, at MetLife Stadium; the score by quarter was Chiefs 17-3-0-3, Jets 0-12-8-0.
The Jets trailed by as much as 17 points (17-0) and tied the game at 20 heading into the fourth quarter.
Patrick Mahomes threw for just 200 yards and one touchdown with two interceptions, but made clutch plays late, including a 24-yard run on 3rd & 22.
Zach Wilson threw for 245 yards and two touchdowns, but his fumble at the Jets' 47 with 7:24 left, recovered by Chiefs DT Tershawn Wharton, proved decisive.
Harrison Butker kicked a 26-yard field goal with 10:51 left to put the Chiefs ahead 23-20; he also hit two 37-yarders earlier.
Isiah Pacheco rushed for 115 yards and a touchdown, including a 48-yard TD run with a block from Trey Smith.
Travis Kelce had a quiet game with six receptions for 60 yards despite the attention around Taylor Swift attending.
Noah Gray caught a 34-yard touchdown from Mahomes for his first TD of the season, making it 17-0.

The Jets scored a safety on a face mask penalty on Chiefs RT Jawaan Taylor in the end zone, and Zach Wilson hit CJ Uzomah for a 1-yard TD and Allen Lazard for a 10-yard TD, then ran in the two-point conversion.
Jets LB CJ Mosley and SS Ashton Davis each intercepted Mahomes in the first half.
A controversial defensive holding call on a Mahomes interception at 3rd & 20 gave the Chiefs an automatic first down with 4:29 left; Jets coach Robert Saleh protested.
Mahomes slid at the one-yard line on a late scramble to close out the game.
NBC broadcast the game with Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark; kickoff was 8:20 p.m. ET.
Entering the game, Kansas City sought a third straight win after a season-opening loss to the Lions, while the Jets sought to avoid a third straight loss after a Week 1 win over the Bills.
